title: Living things suited to their homes

steps.say: A habitat is the place where a living thing lives. It gives food, water and shelter.

figure.alt: A pond, a forest, a desert and the Arctic.

steps.say: Living things have features that suit their habitat. We say they are adapted.
A camel has wide feet for sand and can go days without water. A polar bear has thick fur and fat for the cold.

figure.alt: A camel and a polar bear.

steps.say: Plants are adapted too. A cactus stores water in its thick stem.

figure.alt: A cactus with a thick stem.

steps.say: Small habitats matter too. Woodlice live under logs because it is dark and damp.
People can harm habitats with litter and pollution. We can help by planting trees and recycling.

check.prompt: Which animal is suited to a very cold habitat?

options.why: Camels are suited to hot deserts.

hints: A cold habitat needs animals that keep warm.
Which animal lives near the North Pole?
check.explanation: Polar bears have thick fur and a layer of fat to keep warm in the Arctic.
